description_preview:
Description
As part of the AWS Applied AI Solutions organization, our vision is to provide business applications leveraging Amazon's unique experience and expertise, that are used by millions of companies worldwide to manage day-to-day operations. We will accomplish this by accelerating our customers' success through delivery of intuitive and differentiated technology solutions which solve enduring business challenges. We blend vision with curiosity and Amazon's real-world experience to build opinionated, turnkey solutions. Where customers prefer to buy over build, we become their trusted partner with solutions that are no-brainers to buy and easy to use.
Amazon Connect is an AI-powered customer experience solution that enables superior outcomes at a lower cost. Since its 2017 public launch, Amazon Connect has become an AI leader, transforming how organizations of all types interact with their customers.
The Connect Telecom Engineering team is responsible for provisioning and maintaining connectivity to global telecom carriers, managing the backend telecom infrastructure, and troubleshooting customer issues related to telephony. Our team owns the Session Border Controller (SBC) service used to route calls between Amazon Connect and telecom carriers, ensuring reliable delivery of voice services and telecommunications systems that connect millions of customer interactions worldwide.
We have a rapidly growing customer base and an exciting charter that includes solving highly complex engineering and algorithmic problems in the telephony domain. We are looking for a passionate and talented Software Development Engineer to join us to innovate on the telecom infrastructure that powers Amazon Connect's voice capabilities. The position represents a rare opportunity to be part of a fast-growing business and help shape the technology and product as we grow. You will play a crucial role in developing next-generation telecom systems, and get the opportunity to design and deliver scalable, resilient systems while maintaining a constant customer focus.
Amazon Connect Customer is an agentic solution that helps enterprises deliver exceptional customer experiences at every touchpoint. Amazon Connect Customer's underlying telephony provides superior reliability, quality, and cost-effectiveness through connections to 40+ carriers on the AWS global backbone. Through this network, customers access inbound number coverage across 160 countries, in-country outbound calling in 60+ countries, and international dialing for 200+ countries, eliminating the need to manage legacy dependencies like separate carrier contracts, on-premises session border controllers, or per-trunk capacity planning. Amazon Connect Telephony is the target end-state architecture for all deployments and natively supports instance-to-instance transfer, shared trunking, and external voice transfer to accommodate complex migrations.
Key job responsibilities
As a developer on our team, you'll own code end-to-end from design to development, and work closely with technical leaders within the team and across AWS. You'll have a sound understanding of computer science fundamentals and practical industry experience, working across the stack with technologies involving SIP/VoIP, modern web services, SOA, NoSQL databases, and distributed systems at scale.
A day in the life
Evaluate design decisions that make telecom systems secure, scalable, fault-tolerant, and highly available with low latency.
Implement software solutions for carrier connectivity, call routing, and telecom infrastructure automation.
Improve the operational excellence of the services the team owns, including the SBC platform and carrier management systems.
Provide cross-team impact by mentoring others, participating in operations, design reviews, document reviews, and contributing to team/org goals.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.
Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

title: SDE II , AWS IoT Fleet Management
reason: Stack +18; Title fit +12; Title stack +7; Entry +15; US +10
description_preview:
Description
As part of the AWS Applied AI Solutions organization, we have a vision to provide business applications, leveraging Amazon’s unique experience and expertise, that are used by millions of companies worldwide to manage day-to-day operations. We will accomplish this by accelerating our customers’ businesses through delivery of intuitive and differentiated technology solutions that solve enduring business challenges. We blend vision with curiosity and Amazon’s real-world experience to build opinionated, turnkey solutions. Where customers prefer to buy over build, we become their trusted partner with solutions that are no-brainers to buy and easy to use.
AWS IoT is building the infrastructure to deliver AI from the cloud to the physical world. Our Physical AI team is developing services that provision, deploy, monitor, and secure AI software across every processor inside autonomous machines including robots, vehicles, drones, agricultural equipment, and industrial workcells operating in environments with limited or no cloud connectivity.
We are looking for a Software Development Engineer II to own and drive the design and delivery of core subsystems in our edge-first fleet management platform for Physical AI. You will design and build systems that operate reliably without cloud connectivity handling offline provisioning, state reconciliation on reconnect, staged fleet-wide rollouts, atomic rollback across multi-processor machines, and secure over-the-air (OTA) delivery of AI models and software to heterogeneous processor topologies. Your systems must be correct when disconnected, consistent when reconnected, and resilient when partially connected. You will also develop cloud-side services that orchestrate, monitor, and coordinate with fleets of edge devices, ensuring seamless interaction between cloud control planes and disconnected or intermittently connected hardware. You will write high-performance code, working across the hardware–software boundary to debug issues that span operating systems, runtimes, networks, and physical devices. You will independently own substantial subsystems end to end from writing the design document through implementation, testing, and production operation.
You will also mentor junior engineers, raise the bar on design quality, and help shape the technical direction of the platform. This is an opportunity to build foundational infrastructure for a new category of AWS services delivering intelligence to the physical world at scale.
Key job responsibilities
Design, build, and operate core subsystems of an edge-first fleet management platform, spanning offline provisioning, state reconciliation on reconnect, staged fleet-wide rollouts, and atomic rollback across multi-processor machines
Develop cloud-side services that orchestrate, monitor, and coordinate with fleets of edge devices, ensuring reliable interaction between cloud control planes and disconnected or intermittently connected hardware
Build secure over-the-air (OTA) delivery pipelines for AI models and software across heterogeneous processor topologies
Write and review high-performance, production-quality code, and debug issues that span operating systems, runtimes, networks, and physical devices
Author design documents for new subsystems and drive them independently from proposal through implementation, testing, and production operation
Define and uphold correctness guarantees for disconnected, reconnecting, and partially connected system states
Participate in on-call rotation, troubleshoot production issues, and drive root-cause fixes for the platform
Mentor junior engineers and raise the engineering bar through code review, design review, and technical guidance
Collaborate with product, hardware, and adjacent platform teams to define requirements and integration points for new fleet management capabilities
Contribute to the technical roadmap and architectural direction of the platform as it scales to new device types and processor topologies
A day in the life
Your day starts by checking dashboards — on-call weeks bring pages like an OTA rollback spike; sprint weeks lead into standup with a feature update. Mid-morning often means design review, debating edge cases like reconciling conflicting state after a multi-day disconnect. Sprint weeks give focused coding blocks — building rollback logic across processors, pairing on race conditions. On-call weeks fill that time with live debugging across hardware and software, plus maintenance like patching dependencies. Afternoons bring CR reviews and mentoring a junior engineer through root-causing a bug. You close by updating Taskei and reviewing a peer's design doc.

If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Software Engineer, Cloud + AI
Swish Robotics · San Francisco · On-site · Full-time
Swish builds a countertop robot that actually cooks. You put in a pod or your own ingredients and it hands you a finished meal. The first units are in customers' kitchens now, and every one of them talks to AWS every day.
We are very early with a functional robot, real users, and a lot of the system still to be built. This role is for an engineer who wants to shape the cloud and AI side of the product while it is still small enough to shape.
Where you would contribute
The fleet platform on AWS. The cloud that every robot depends on: how units are identified and updated in the field, how we keep development and production apart, how we know something is wrong before a customer does, and how we see what the fleet is doing.
The data platform. Every cook produces data. Some of it lands in S3 today; there is a lot more to do to make it queryable and to turn it into training and evaluation sets.
AI in the loop. We want the robot to cook well from what it senses rather than from a hand-tuned model per dish. That needs training pipelines, evaluation, packaging for the device, delivery over the air, and a feedback loop from the fleet back into training.
Product features that live in the cloud. The app, the customer experience, and the tools our culinary team uses all have a backend. Small features, real users, fast turnaround.
Units in homes. When a customer's robot misbehaves, someone looks at its logs and decides what to ship. Everyone here is on deployment duty.
What we need from you
You have shipped and operated production systems on AWS, and you have done it with infrastructure as code (CDK, Terraform, or CloudFormation). You have worked with connected devices, or something close enough that IoT Core, MQTT, device shadows and OTA are not new words to you.
You write Python well. You are comfortable on a Linux box you cannot see: systemd, journals, Ansible, a device that reboots mid-command.
You take security seriously without being precious about it: PKI, secrets management, least privilege, what a stolen device can and cannot leak.
You can take a trained model and make it real: data pipelines, evaluation that means something, packaging for an edge device, a rollout you can roll back. You do not need to be a researcher. You need to be the person who makes the researcher's work run on every machine.
You have worked somewhere small enough that you owned outcomes, not tickets.

Flutter or Dart. Embedded experience. Computer vision or sensor fusion. Observability and analytics tooling.

description_preview:
About Hero Instruments
Hero Instruments builds the tools engineers use to ship Bluetooth LE products: BLE Hero on iOS and Android, BLE Hero Workbench in VS Code, Harald, who runs the Workbench for you and reads the logs when something fails, and the BLE Hero Probe, the HCI controller that plugs into all of it. Everything we make is built by people who spend their days at a bench with a dev kit, a phone, and a sniffer, for people who do the same. We are a small team, and we would rather teach than promote.
The Role
You are the engineer we build for. You own the Bluetooth LE firmware on a product from the first advertising packet to the last DFU, and you know the cost of doing it with a scanner app on the phone, a sniffer capture in one window, a Python script for the boring parts, and a serial terminal for everything else.
At Hero Instruments you will do that work every day, on our reference firmware, on the Probe, across the SDKs our customers use, and everything you learn will end up in the product. When a connection drops for a reason nobody can explain, you read the trace, find it, and make sure Harald finds it next time.
What you'll
Bring up new BLE peripherals on real silicon: advertising, connection establishment, the GATT table, pairing and bonding, privacy. Characterize how each behaves against iOS and Android centrals, not just against another dev kit.
Debug at the protocol level. Root-cause disconnects, failed connections, stalled throughput, and pairing failures from HCI traces and air captures. Know why a 0x08 is not a 0x3E, and document each failure mode precisely enough that Harald can recognize it.
Tune connection interval, peripheral latency, supervision timeout, PHY, LL data length, and ATT MTU against a real throughput or power budget, and prove it with measurements.
Own DFU/OTA end to end across vendor mechanisms (MCUboot with MCUmgr/SMP over BLE, ESP-IDF OTA, others as customers need them), including the failure and rollback paths.
Build repeatable test sequences that exercise a device end to end on real hardware, then turn them into automated regression that runs against racks of devices, not simulators.
Own the firmware for the BLE Hero Probe: an nRF52840 running as a raw HCI controller over USB CDC. Transport reliability and throughput, flow control, and the Probe's own update path are yours.
Maintain reference peripheral firmware across the SDKs our customers live in: nRF Connect SDK/Zephyr and ESP-IDF first, then STM32WB, Silicon Labs, and TI SimpleLink as the roadmap demands. These double as our test targets and our teaching examples.
Write. Protocol-level explanations, example workflows, and docs that transfer knowledge, in the terminology the spec uses.
Work across the boundary with the extension (TypeScript) and mobile (Swift/Kotlin) teams: reproduce phone-side failures on firmware and decide which layer actually owns the fix.
What you've done
At least 2 years of experience with Zephyr
Shipped Bluetooth LE firmware on at least one product people bought, in C, on Cortex-M or ESP32-class silicon.
Gone deep on at least one BLE stack. nRF Connect SDK/Zephyr preferred; ESP-IDF (NimBLE or Bluedroid), Silicon Labs, TI SimpleLink, or STM32WB also count.
Can walk a connection from advertising through connection establishment, service discovery, and pairing, and point to where each step fails in practice.
Read HCI logs and sniffer captures without a translator. btmon, Wireshark, nRF Sniffer or equivalent are in your daily toolkit.
Tuned connection parameters, PHY, and DLE/MTU for a real target, and learned what iOS and Android will and won't accept.
Implemented or maintained a DFU/OTA path in production.
Comfortable in VS Code and git with CMake/west or idf.py, a J-Link or equivalent, RTT or UART logging, and a logic analyzer within reach.
Python for test automation and tooling.
Nice to have
TypeScript, or experience with the VS Code extension API.
Host-stack internals: you have written, ported, or debugged inside a Bluetooth host stack (Zephyr host, NimBLE, Bumble, BlueZ).
iOS Core Bluetooth or Android BLE experience. You have been on the phone side of a failure too.
Extended and periodic advertising, LE Coded PHY range work, LE Audio or isochronous channels.
Bluetooth SIG qualification, DTM/RF test, regulatory.
Hardware-in-the-loop CI at scale, and the flakiness triage that comes with it.
You have published something that taught other engineers BLE.

Orchard’s engineering team values clarity, collaboration, and ownership. Our team builds the systems behind Orchard’s website and the tools that help agents reach new customers. We focus on helping people explore homes, book consultations, and connect with our agents. Our site serves over 150k unique visitors each month and sees about 700k pageviews. Debug and improve core services to make them faster and more reliable as we prepare for national growth over the next 12-18 months.

Write clean, tested code that’s easy to understand and maintain.

Take part in on-call rotations and own the systems you build.
Work with a small team that values communication, trust, and practical solutions.
Use AI coding tools like Claude Code, Copilot, and Codex as part of your daily workflow to build and ship features efficiently.
Comfortable reviewing code you didn't write

At least 2+ years of experience as a software engineer.
Strong skills in at least one language relevant to our stack (Python, TypeScript, or Go), with solid knowledge of APIs and data modeling.
Experience with tools like AWS, Postgres, SQL, Kafka, Airflow, Docker, or CircleCI is a plus.
Experience directing AI coding tools effectively
A low-ego, problem-solving mindset. You take ownership, improve what you touch, and ask for help when something doesn't add up.
Interest in a hands-on team where engineers ship quickly and have real impact.

Collaborate with Software Development Engineers, Product Engineers, and Product Managers to design, enhance, and validate REST APIs for geospatial workflows in ArcGIS Enterprise across multiple deployment environments (Windows, Linux, Kubernetes)

Advocate for users and developers within the software development team, ensuring APIs are intuitive, consistent, and built to support customer workflows
Participate in project planning, contributing to scope definition, timelines, and delivery milestones
Coordinate and communicate REST API features, updates, and changes with internal teams across engineering, documentation, support, and product management

Our

has been crafted to simulate our Engineering Associate Programme so that you can understand what a career in Technology and Engineering at LSEG would really be like.
To be eligible, you must be in your junior year of your undergraduate studies due to
complete all the requirements of your course summer 2028

D&A, Markets, Risk Intelligence, FTSE Russell, I&C Engineering
functions.

We are passionate about recruiting people who are interested in pursuing a career within Technology and would like to learn about the full breadth of our business – and are interested in playing a part of our development, as it grows and diversifies.

A curiosity for data and an ability to analyse information to draw conclusions and propose solutions.
Individuals who are able to connect the dots and think creatively.

People who can collaborate with others, using their strong communication skills in the process.
You will stand out to us if you can demonstrate and recognise that what you achieve is equally important to how you achieve it.

30th October, however we recommend an early application because we consider candidates on a rolling basis. Due to the volume of applications, we might close the applications earlier, so we recommend an early application.

The first stage of the recruitment process involves making an application and submitting your resume.
The second stage is completing Technical and Coding Assessment. This technical assessment is designed to evaluate your coding ability, logical reasoning and problem-solving skills.
The next stage of the application process is an untimed Immersive Online Assessment. The assessment is designed to give you an insight into what it’s like to work at LSEG.
The third stage is a video interview where you will answer a series of questions using a strength-based-interview style
The final stage is a virtual half day assessment centre which involves several different types of exercises – further information is provided at the point of invite.

one application If you make more than one application, we will review your first application only.
Please note, all our assessment centres are held virtually.

We are looking for a Controls Programmer who thrives on solving problems and making machines move.
Position Summary
If you enjoy turning electrical and mechanical concepts into reliable, working automation, this is a role where your contribution will be visible every day. We are seeking a Controls Programmer I to join our team and help program, debug, and commission custom machinery. You will work alongside experienced mechanical and electrical technicians to solve real-world problems, validate machine operation, and make sure each system is ready to perform.
This opportunity is ideal for an early-career controls professional who wants to strengthen their PLC programming skills while gaining meaningful exposure to machine sequencing, electrical systems, operator interfaces, documentation, and field service.
Key Responsibilities
Write and debug PLC code in accordance with work instructions, project specifications, and customer requirements.
Program graphic user interfaces that help operators interact confidently with automated equipment.
Partner with mechanical and electrical technicians to confirm machine sequences and achieve reliable system functionality.
Test switches, cylinders, actuators, and other devices to verify that every component performs as intended.
Maintain accurate project documentation, including drawings, parts lists, calibration data, wire lists, and specifications.
Support machine-manual development and occasional field service work for installation, modification, and system support.
Contribute ideas that improve processes, quality, and the way our team works.
Qualifications
Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related engineering discipline.
A working knowledge of ladder logic programming for a variety of PLC platforms.
Familiarity with PLC networks, communications, and hardware and software interfaces.
Knowledge of foundational electrical concepts, including PNP and NPN switches, AC and DC circuits, E-Stop circuits, and stepper or servo motor function.
The ability to read and understand electrical prints and technical documents.
A safety-first mindset and willingness to work in an active, hands-on environment, including occasional travel when needed.

description_preview:
About The Company
General Matter enriches uranium.
We are designing, building, and operating the world’s lowest-cost enrichment services, here in the US.
In the process, we are restoring America’s ability to produce nuclear fuel to power AI, advanced manufacturing and critical industries our country relies on to remain competitive.
Fuel drives the cost of advanced reactor electricity production, and enrichment drives the cost of the fuel that advanced reactors consume. Reliable, low-cost enrichment is the catalyst for the nuclear Renaissance now under way.
Our mission is to make nuclear not only the cleanest and safest source of baseload power, but also the most affordable. We believe abundant nuclear energy will lead to a post-scarcity society.
We were incubated inside Founders Fund, like Anduril and Palantir before us, and are backed by over a dozen of the world's top venture capital firms.
Our lean, world-class team of engineers and operators is applying a first-principles approach to solving the problem of nuclear fuel production.
We are a mission-driven company with a culture of urgency, accountability, and transparency.
Help us build a high-energy society by making the cleanest, safest form of baseload energy the most affordable.
About This Role
As a Motor Controls Engineer, you will design, develop, and implement the control algorithms and software that run the electric motors, drives, and motion systems at the core of our enrichment technology. This role spans control-oriented modeling, motor and motion control design, state estimation and monitoring, and hands-on integration and calibration across simulation, bench, and integrated hardware. You will work with hardware throughout the lifecycle, from early prototypes through deployed systems, partnering closely with power electronics, firmware, systems integration, and mechanical teams.
Open to multiple levels of experience.
Responsibilities
Develop control-oriented models of motors, drives, and rotating machinery for analysis, control design, and estimation.
Design and implement motor and motion control algorithms to maximize system capability, performance, and flexibility.
Develop estimation and monitoring algorithms to maximize system safety and reliability, including state, speed, and fault estimation.
Evaluate novel subsystems and architectures related to motor control and drive systems to inform product decisions.
Work with power electronics, firmware, and integration engineers to test, debug, and calibrate algorithms in simulation and on hardware.
Ensure stability and performance of algorithms using software-in-the-loop (SIL) and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) tools, on the bench and in integrated systems.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate motor controls with mechanical, power electronics, firmware, and process systems.
Develop technical documentation and specifications for internal use, vendors, and contractors.
Support testing, commissioning, and ongoing system improvements across R&D and facility deployments.
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Controls Engineering, or a related discipline.
Strong background in first-principles linear systems analysis, state estimation, and control design.
Fundamental understanding of electric motors and drive systems, such as field-oriented control, sensorless control, and power electronics and inverters.
Demonstrated ability to design, analyze, implement, test, and debug control systems from the ground up in real-world applications.
Proficiency with engineering development tools such as MATLAB/Simulink and Python, and with software development in C/C++ for embedded or real-time control.
Ability to perform trade studies, reason from first principles, and make sound engineering decisions with incomplete information.
Excellent problem-solving and communication skills for cross-functional collaboration.
Evidence of exceptional ability (prior projects, portfolio of work, completed products, etc).
Preferred Skills And Experience
Expertise in advanced control and estimation techniques and optimal control.
Experience with high-speed motors, precision motion control, or rotating machinery.
Experience with power electronics, motor drives, and real-time embedded control implementation.
Experience developing control systems for industrial, R&D, or other regulated or safety-critical environments.
Advanced degrees.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, multidisciplinary environment, balancing technical rigor with practical constraints.
Additional Requirements
Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary.
Equal Opportunity Employer
General Matter is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with General Matter is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.
Compensation And Benefits
The base salary range for this role is
$ 120,000-$160,000
annually.
Compensation bands are determined by role, level, location, and alignment with market data. Individual level and base pay is determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on job-related skills, education, experience, technical capabilities and internal equity. Please note that the stated salary range is an estimate and may be adjusted based on market conditions, business needs, or other factors. In addition to base salary, for full-time hires, you may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of stock options, and access to medical, vision & dental coverage as well as access to a 401(k) retirement plan.

Master’s degree or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

Experience designing or building on-device permission systems, access control frameworks, sandboxing, secure IPC, service isolation, least-privilege architectures, or privacy-preserving controls for sensor-rich devices.
Experience securing on-device AI, ML, or assistant-like systems, including model integrity, sensitive data handling, inference-time privacy, AI feature permissions, local policy enforcement, and protection of model inputs and outputs.

description_preview:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
About The Team
Anduril develops advanced robotic systems that operate at the edge across land, sea, and air. Our team builds the critical systems powering everything from Group 1–3 autonomous aerial systems (such as Ghost, Anvil, Bolt, and Altius) to autonomous Sentry Towers that safeguard borders and critical infrastructure with real-time sensor fusion.
Underpinning these diverse robotic fleets is our
DeviceOS team
, which engineers the unified, highly reliable operating system and hardware-enablement platform that powers all of Anduril's autonomous assets. We take systems from initial schematics and paper sketches to hardened, field-ready robotics deployed in the most challenging operational environments on Earth.
About The Job
Underneath our airframes and Sentry Towers are custom carrier boards, embedded ARM architectures, and NVIDIA Jetson modules integrated with an intense array of hardware: electro-optical/infrared cameras, radars, CAN-connected sensor nodes, GPS, flight controllers, radios, and high-power motor drivers.
Between the silicon vendor’s raw Board Support Package (BSP) and our autonomous mission software sits a layer that must be owned deliberately: the boot chain, device trees, kernel drivers, and the guarantee that every piece of hardware deterministically enumerates and operates when our image boots.
In this role, you will own the boundary where custom hardware meets software. You will customize vendor BSPs and evaluate upstream changes. You will debug boot end-to-end—from firmware (EDK2/U-Boot) through unified kernel images to an encrypted root filesystem running at the tactical edge. You are the engineer who can read a schematic to diagnose a bus fault, remediate a kernel CVE on deployed hardware, and write the platform drivers that keep our robots flying and monitoring.
In this role, you will maintain and support a large deployed fleet by writing fixes for existing hardware and boot chains. This work is critical to our operations: a firmware regression is not just a failing test, it is a physical unit someone has to service in the field.
What You’ll Do
Own the Boot Path: Own the boot sequence end-to-end on deployed compute: low-level firmware, U-Boot/UEFI, unified kernel images, initrd, encrypted storage unlock, and handoff to a running NixOS environment. Debug boot failures on hardware via remote support.
Customize & Sustain Vendor BSPs: Reconcile vendor BSPs (Tegra/Jetson Linux, NXP, etc.) with modern NixOS package sets. Produce kernel and device tree patches when hardware requires custom behavior, and forward-port these changes across OS baseline upgrades.
Guarantee Deterministic Hardware Availability: Ensure all peripherals—cameras, radars, motor controllers, CAN networks, and radios—are reliably enumerated, correctly named, and fully operational across boots and platform upgrades.
Sustain a Long-Lived Baseline: Keep the existing signed boot chain and disk encryption working as the firmware, kernels, and package sets change underneath them. Triage and remediate CVEs in vendor kernels and low-level system components on our systems already deployed in the field.
Automate & Validate: Build and maintain automated Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) test suites to catch regressions in power states, bus communication, and platform stability before code hits flight or field hardware.
Perform Deep Hardware/Software Root-Cause Analysis: Diagnose intermittent bus errors, thermal and power throttling issues, kernel panics, and boot hangs using serial consoles, logic analyzers, dmesg, and hardware schematics.
Be the Upstream: Triage upstream kernel and vendor BSP issues, produce the patch when no upstream fix is coming, and carry that patch set forward as the platform moves.
Required Qualifications
4+ years of professional embedded Linux platform, sustainment of deployed embedded Linux platforms, or kernel-adjacent integration experience.
Deep understanding of the embedded Linux boot chain: firmware/bootloaders (U-Boot, EDK2), device trees, kernel command line, initrd/initramfs, and root filesystem assembly.
Strong programming skills in C (for kernel/driver development and BSP patching) along with proficiency in Rust or C++ for userspace platform integration and services.
Hands-on experience debugging hardware at the bench: using serial consoles, reading schematics and component datasheets, and tracing issues to the board level.
Experience maintaining software deployed on real-world hardware, where updates must be safe, resilient to bricking, and strictly validated against regressions.
U.S. Person status is required due to export control regulations (ITAR/EAR), with eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance.
Preferred Qualifications
Nix / NixOS Experience: Direct experience with declarative systems (Nix/NixOS) for embedded builds; or deep expertise in Yocto/Buildroot paired with an appetite to transition to modern, reproducible paradigms.
NVIDIA Jetson / Tegra Depth: Hands-on experience with JetPack, Jetson Linux BSP, Tegra boot architecture, or CUDA compute runtime integration.
Low-Level Platform Security: Practical implementation of hardware root-of-trust, secure boot, HAB/AHAB, or measured boot (TPM).

Support ongoing test automation improvement efforts, including modularization and scalability enhancements.

The Platform Engineering and Emerging Technologies (PEET) team is hiring for a Software Development Engineer to support the development of AWS Secret Cloud for Industry! You'll design, build, deploy, and monitor features to enhance the user experience for our customers. You'll build tools and systems to provide a highly-available and resilient platform for our customers' and our team's workloads.
Would you like to implement innovative cloud computing solutions and solve the world's most complex technical problems? Do you have a deep passion and desire to engineer and operate the world's largest cloud computing infrastructure to build a better world for future generations?
This is an exciting opportunity to use the latest cloud computing technologies to help U.S. Government agencies implement innovative cloud computing solutions and solve technical problems. AWS established a specialized group of service teams responsible for the work we are doing with the U.S. Intelligence Community. We are building some of the largest and most complex distributed systems in the world, and we need adaptable people to help us implement and operate them.
This position requires that after start, the selected candidate obtain and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph or commensurate clearance for each government agency for which they perform AWS work.
Key job responsibilities
Design, build, deploy, and monitor components of the AWS Secret Cloud for Industry service.
This position involves on-call responsibilities, typically for one week in every six. We don’t like getting paged in the middle of the night or on the weekend, so we work to ensure that our systems are fault tolerant. When we do get paged, we work together to resolve the root cause so that we don’t get paged for the same issue twice.
About The Team
Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.
AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS)
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.
Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.
Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.
Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor's degree, or CSSLP (Certified Secure Software Lifecycle Professional)
3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
Experience programming with at least one software programming language
Preferred Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent
3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers.
